author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, named first name then last name. All specialties appear on one page. The page is reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every one of them is listed under its stored name.
Given a specialty that veterinarians hold, when the specialty directory is opened, then each holder is named by first name then last name.
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is named nowhere on it.
Given every specialty the clinic knows, when the specialty directory is opened, then all of them appear on one page, with no paging.
Given any page of the system, when it is rendered, then it carries no link to the specialty directory.
Edge case 3: a specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, shown as held by none.
Edge case 4: specialties are listed in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians within each.
Edge case 5: when the clinic knows no specialty at all, the specialty directory opens and reports that there is none.
Edge case 6: the specialty directory carries the navigation every page carries, as REQ-SYS-001 requires; nothing in that navigation points at it.
Edge case 7: wording the specialty directory introduces is present in every supported language, as REQ-LANG-002 requires.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application — NG-2 is unchanged, and the specialty directory is read-only.
A navigation entry or a link from any other page. The product owner names a visible entry point as a possible follow-up request.
Searching or filtering the specialty directory — NG-9 is unchanged.
Paging the specialty directory, unlike the veterinarian directory of REQ-VET-001.
notes: Product channel closed for this slice; no further product answer is available. Narrowest readings taken where the request was silent, each recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md: (1) order of specialties and of veterinarians within each — a stable order, matching REQ-VET-001 edge case 1, alphabetical unconfirmed; (2) a specialty no veterinarian holds is listed, since the view lists every specialty the clinic knows; (3) an empty clinic-wide specialty list opens rather than fails. REQ-LANG-002 makes new wording a translation obligation across every supported language — the language bundles are in scope for this slice. REQ-SYS-001 keeps the navigation on the new page while nothing in that navigation points at it; the no-link acceptance bullet guards that pairing. Provenance: docs/prd.md marks REQ-VET-003 as the one requirement stated by the product owner rather than derived from observed behavior.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and adds the codebase's first derived read model: the store holds Vet-to-Specialty with no inverse, so the specialty-first page cannot render a persisted entity straight into a template. Placement, ordering, caching, and the product-fixed address /specialties.html are decided in docs/adr/2026-08-08-specialty-directory-read-model.md. Grouping lives in a plain, MVC-free type rather than the controller, so architecture-principles.md 'Web controller' row (no new business rule in a controller) holds. Repository, controller, and template placement follow the existing feature-package shape (system-design.md Package Structure); the lookup repository mirrors PetTypeRepository.
integration_points: New route GET /specialties.html served by SpecialtyController in the vet package; the address is product-stated, not a design choice.

New SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> with a single read method (JPQL or derived), mirroring PetTypeRepository. Keep the interface narrow: no save/delete surface, so NG-2 holds mechanically.
Holders come from the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(); Vet.specialties is EAGER, so no lazy access at render time (open-in-view is disabled).

New template templates/vets/specialtyList.html replaces the layout fragment with a menu key that matches no menuItem in fragments/layout.html. That renders the shared navigation with nothing active and adds no link, satisfying the no-link criterion without editing layout.html.

New message keys (page heading, empty-clinic wording) go into all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages/; 'specialties' and 'none' already exist. The bundle-parity test enforces REQ-LANG-002.

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository with a single read method - the shape SpecialtyRepository follows
layout fragment call whose second argument is the active-menu key; pass a non-matching key for the specialty directory
existing sort-in-Java of specialties by name - the ordering precedent the read model extends

risks.risk: Grouping keyed on the Specialty object silently produces duplicate or empty entries. BaseEntity, NamedEntity, Person, Specialty, and Vet override neither equals nor hashCode, so equality is identity, and the specialty read and the (cached) vet read return separate instances of the same row.
risks.mitigation: Key the grouping on the specialty identifier, and render the stored name. A test with a specialty reachable from both reads pins this.

risks.risk: Annotating the specialty read @Cacheable("vets") collides with VetRepository.findAll(): two no-argument methods under one cache name share SimpleKey.EMPTY, so one call returns the other's type.
risks.mitigation: Leave the specialty read uncached. Introducing a cache for it requires a distinct name declared in CacheConfiguration.

risks.risk: VetRepository.findAll() may return a cached, request-shared Collection<Vet>. Sorting or otherwise mutating it in place corrupts state for later requests.
risks.mitigation: Assemble with read-only stream operations into new collections; never sort or modify the returned collection or the Vet instances.

risks.risk: Ordering delegated to SQL diverges per vendor. The PostgreSQL-vs-H2 case-sensitivity split is already a Known Defect for owner search (system-design.md Known Defects).
risks.mitigation: Sort in Java inside the read model: specialties by name, holders by last name then first name, with a deterministic tie-break. The order is then identical on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, and unit-testable.

risks.risk: A package-private read-model type breaks Thymeleaf property access, which reflects over the model attribute's class.
risks.mitigation: Declare the read-model type public, as Vet is. SpecialtyController stays package-private, matching VetController.

risks.risk: Reusing the 'vets' menu key highlights the veterinarian navigation entry on the specialty page, misreporting where the reader is.
risks.mitigation: Pass a key that matches no menuItem; assert that the rendered page contains no href to /specialties.html.

notes: Deviations from the prd-entry file_targets, all architectural and mine to decide: (1) a separate SpecialtyController rather than a second mapping on VetController - the owner package's precedent is one controller per resource, and VetController stays focused; (2) tests land in SpecialtyControllerTests plus a plain SpecialtyDirectoryTests rather than in VetControllerTests, since the grouping is testable without MVC; (3) VetController and VetRepository are unchanged - VetRepository.findAll() is reused as-is. Acceptance criteria and test names from the prd-entry are unchanged and binding. Product channel closed: the three narrowest readings (stable order, unheld specialty listed, empty clinic opens) are taken as given, and alphabetical is the design's choice of stable order. docs/system-design.md is deliberately not edited in this dispatch: it states current working-tree state under a provenance banner, so its Contracts rows and the /specialties.html address land through doc-sync once the code exists. Until then the ADR carries the address and the decision. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: review-plan-engine
rationale: risk triggers present (multi-module, oversize, design-revision); full battery

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectory.of documents the identity-equality hazard (grouping by specialty id, not the Specialty instance) and both comparators explain their tie-break rationale — javadoc carries real design context, not restatement
SpecialtyRepository javadoc explains why the read carries no @Cacheable (would collide with the shared 'vets' cache key), matching the ADR's stated constraint
Records used correctly for the read model: SpecialtyDirectory and the nested SpecialtyHolders are immutable with List.copyOf defensive copies in compact constructors

SpecialtyController mirrors VetController's shape (constructor injection, @Controller, single @GetMapping returning a view name) so the new controller reads as familiar to anyone who has seen the existing one
Test suites in both SpecialtyControllerTests and SpecialtyDirectoryTests use AssertJ, BDD-style names, and factory methods (radiology()/vetHolding()) for construction; no magic literals
checkFormat passes clean; messages.properties additions are present and consistent across all locale files

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: New endpoint GET /specialties.html is read-only: no request parameters, no path variables, no request body, so the change opens no new input boundary and needs no binder disallow list

Data access uses Spring Data repository derived reads only (SpecialtyRepository.findAll, VetRepository.findAll) with @Transactional(readOnly = true); no string-concatenated or native query text is introduced

Output escaping holds: specialtyList.html renders every stored value through th:text (specialty name, holder first/last name) and every literal through message keys; no th:utext, inline JavaScript, or DOM injection anywhere in the new template

No widening of the exposed data surface: specialty names and veterinarian names are already served unauthenticated by GET /vets.html and GET /vets; the directory is a re-projection of data already public at the baseline
No new endpoint that mutates state and no change to management-endpoint exposure; the controller documents what the page exposes
No secrets introduced: the ten message-bundle additions are UI strings only, and no credential, connection string, or key literal appears anywhere in the diff
No file, path, resource-name, or deserialization operation is introduced; the view name is a compile-time constant, not request-derived
Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, settings.gradle, and the gradle/ directory are absent from the change set, so no new or upgraded dependency enters and no CVE surface is added
SpecialtyDirectory.of treats both reads as read-only inputs and copies collections defensively in the record constructors, so the shared vets cache cannot be mutated through the directory

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: testing-principles.md's Three-Tier Data Naming convention requires irrelevant (Tier 2) values to carry a SOME_/ANY_ prefix or come from an anonymous factory that auto-generates them, and meaningful (Tier 1) values to be named by role. Every vetHolding(...) call in both files passes a bare integer literal for the vet id. In most tests the id is irrelevant scaffolding (e.g. vetHolding("Helen", "Leary", 2, radiology)) and should not require the caller to invent a number. In theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderHoldersSharingANameByTheirIdentifier (SpecialtyDirectoryTests.java:110-119) the ids 9 and 2 are Tier 1 — they are exactly what the test's outcome (ordering) depends on — yet appear as unnamed literals rather than role-named constants (e.g. LOWER_ID/HIGHER_ID).
findings.fix: Change the vetHolding(...) factory in both test files to auto-generate the id (e.g. an incrementing counter or a fixed default) and drop the id parameter from call sites where it is irrelevant, keeping an explicit-id overload only for tests where the id is the value under test (the identifier tie-break case), and name those meaningful ids by role instead of using bare literals.

AssertJ used throughout the unit test file; four-phase structure with blank-line separation and no narration comments in both files; construction wrapped in factory methods, never raw constructors; BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming followed consistently

Grouping-by-identifier and case-sensitive-ordering risks flagged in the design-block are each pinned by a dedicated test (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupOnTheStoredIdentityRatherThanTheSpecialtyInstance, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderHoldersSharingANameByTheirIdentifier)

summary: add the read-only specialty directory page

blast_radius.note: Purely additive: three new files in the vet package, one new template, and a one-line message key in each of the ten populated bundles. Not one existing production Java file, template, or build file is modified, so no existing request path changes behavior. No sensitive path is touched, and the new route serves specialty and veterinarian names already published unauthenticated at /vets.html and /vets.

semantic_surprise.note: The read model does exactly what its size and prose suggest, and its three non-obvious choices are deliberate and each pinned by a test: holders are grouped on Specialty.getId() rather than on the entity (which inherits identity equality, so the naive map keyed by Specialty would split one row into two), both comparators carry an id tie-break, and SpecialtyRepository.findAll deliberately omits the cache annotation because a second no-argument cached read under the vets cache would collide on the shared empty key. Defensive copies in both compact constructors and fresh lists in the grouping mean the shared vet cache is never mutated. No inverted condition, no off-by-one, no flipped boundary anywhere in the 31 hunks. The Hindi bundle stores its new line as raw Devanagari while its older lines use unicode escapes, which is cosmetic only: the bundle set is already read as UTF-8 and four other locale files already carry raw UTF-8.

test_adequacy.note: The tests would fail against a broken implementation rather than merely restating it. SpecialtyDirectoryTests drives the identity trap directly by passing two distinct Specialty instances of the same row, and separately pins name order, last-then-first holder order, the id tie-break, an unheld specialty, and the empty clinic. SpecialtyControllerTests renders the real Thymeleaf template through MockMvc and asserts on rendered content, including two negatives that matter: no paging markup and no link to the page's own address. Every done-when bullet in the requirement has a matching assertion.

reviewer_hedging.note: The full four-reviewer battery was dispatched and all four returned approved with zero findings in the second round. Round one produced one blocked doc finding (system-design.md not updated for code that already existed) and one fixable test-data-naming finding; both were reworked and each reviewer named the specific fix delta in its re-approval. No escalate tag, no approval-with-caveats, and no lingering worry is recorded anywhere in the log.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the triaged surface with nothing extra: no navigation link was added (the requirement forbids one), no write path to specialties exists, and no unrelated refactor rode along. The single design revision was a superseding design-block that added docs/adr/README.md to supporting_paths for the autofix audit, not an architectural rethink. The row's build_retries of 0 understates the slice's history, and reading the log rather than the counter resolves it: the two build-failure records are a planned mid-dispatch checkpoint and that same audit-coverage gap, neither a code defect.

rationale: Additive change in one package that modifies no existing code path, with the three genuinely tricky decisions (entity-identity grouping, Java-side ordering, the deliberately uncached read) each documented and pinned by a test a broken implementation would fail.
